Please act as a professional verilog designer.

Implement a module of a 16-bit full adder in combinational logic.

Module name:
    adder_16bit
Input ports:
    a[15:0]: 16-bit input operand A.
    b[15:0]: 16-bit input operand B.
    Cin: Carry-in input. The module name "Cin" is case-sensitive.
Output ports:
    y[15:0]: 16-bit output representing the sum of A and B.
    Co: Carry-out output. The module name "Co" is case-sensitive.

Implementation:
In the adder_16bit module, you need to design a small bit-width adder(8-bit adder), which will be instantiated multiple times. The 8-bit adder module utilizes a series of bit-level adders (full adders) to perform the addition operation.

Give me the complete code.

The Verilator compiler raises a Warning, called UNUSEDSIGNAL, for the below module. The content of the Warning is "Bits of signal are not driven, nor used: 'internal_carry'[7:1]".
Here is the related in-line content with the Warning:

Line 43: wire [7:0] internal_carry;

Here is description of the "UNUSEDSIGNAL":
A Warning that the specified signal is never used/consumed.
For example, you have a wire called `a`, declared as follows:

```sv
wire [3:0] a;
```

But in the operation of a module, you only use 2/4 bits of the wire `a`. For example:

```sv
assign a[1:0] = {1'b0, 1'b1};
```

And you forgot to use the `a[3:2]`. So, that is why this warning is raised.

You should fix this warning by removing unused signals in the declaration of a port, such as:

```sv
wire [1:0] a;
```

Or you can make use of the unused signals that you forgot:

```sv
assign a[3:0] = {1'b0, 1'b1, 1'b0, 1'b1};
```
